P1.evidence: No setter is named anywhere on this call and there is no evidence of a pre-qualification handoff, so P1a drops out. The frame itself was the cleanest four-part delivery in the batch: 'I want to understand your situation. What's going on? Like, what have you tried? Where you're trying to get to? And how can we actually help you get there?' Agreement was sought and given — 'Yeah? Amazing.' / 'Yeah, I can provide all that context, I think.' The open question and the frame were the same move here and it worked; the prospect gave a five-minute structured answer covering history, current state and goal.

P2.evidence: Five clean hits and the nutrition work in particular was excellent — 'Look, it's only two of us over here. Be brutally honest. How does it look like in real life? You don't need to sugarcoat it' produced a genuinely candid answer, and the follow-up separating weekday discipline from social eating found the real pattern. Work, training capacity, current-programme results and energy were all properly asked. But the two checks that mattered most on this specific call both failed. P2c was never asked at all — no health conditions question, no hereditary question. P2d scores partial and only because the prospect volunteered his entire injury history unprompted in the first four minutes; the rep asked clarifying questions about how it happened ('Just from one squatting session?') but never asked the questions that matter for a purchase decision: how bad is it right now, how long has the brace been on, what did the physical therapist say, has anyone cleared you for loaded ballistic work. Age, height and body composition were all volunteered and never requested. Sleep surfaced inside the energy answer rather than being asked.

P3.evidence: Two strong moves. The bridge was well placed and genuinely probing — 'Why do you want to do this? Because you're doing already four things, different things' — which is the right question to a man already spending on four modalities, and it produced the structure gap. And P3c was run properly with a good instinct: 'Apart from the baby thing, what have you been missing out throughout those months and years that you've been injured?' followed by 'Do you miss that, those workouts?' / 'Absolutely.' That surfaced the plyometrics, the basketball and the elite coach, which is the emotional core of the call. Against that, the specific physique target was volunteered rather than asked, nobody else's stake was ever explored — the wife and the planned child came entirely from the prospect — and the rep amplified the baby motive by assertion ('that's actually a very good why. The strongest that can be, your kids') rather than asking who else it impacts. No reflect-back in the scripted form.

P4.evidence: Well run. Past and current attempts were both established, and the rep drilled properly rather than accepting the first answer: 'What do you mean haphazard?', then 'you said you're training with a trainer, right?', then 'Why is that? Why do you think it won't get you [there]?'. That sequence made the prospect name the gap himself in his own words — no structure, no three-month progression, 'it feels random', 'I don't think it's pushing me hard enough'. That is exactly what P4e asks for. Marked down because the present-tense blocker was never named as the injury, which is the actual thing getting in the way, and the 'information isn't the problem' line was not used on a prospect who is unusually well informed and told the rep so.

P5.evidence: Absent. Fourth consecutive sales call in this batch with no consequence frame at all. Here the material was unusually available — a man planning his first child inside a year, in a back brace, who says the window closes when the baby arrives — and the rep let the prospect build his own urgency rather than building it. It closed anyway, which is precisely why this phase keeps getting skipped.

P6.evidence: P6a ran properly and in the right place, before the price: 'if you had this right training, nutrition and accountability from Trevor built around your life, do you feel and do you agree that you would get to that version of Peter from 2018?' P6b was consciously skipped — the rep said out loud 'I think I'll re-ask you about the commitment, so I don't think I need to ask you again', having only run a soft variant earlier ('we want to be 100% sure that you're going to follow through'). P6c is a clear miss and the most consequential scoring line on this call: hesitation surfaced three times — the cardio sufficiency question, 'Do you know if Trevor's worked with anyone with a back injury?', and 'maybe I should wait two weeks so that my back can heal up' — and on each the rep moved forward rather than back. The script's instruction is explicit that hesitation returns you to Phase 5. Here it accelerated the close instead.

P11.evidence: The only complete P11 in the batch and it ran in the correct order. Payment first and confirmed — 'we got the payment'. Onboarding with Trevor booked for 3:15pm the next day after checking the prospect's time zone and working through his availability. Agreement arrival confirmed and signed live, which no other call achieved: 'Could you check your inbox? Did you get the confirmation and the email with the agreement?' / 'Yes, I got it.' / 'I see you already signed the agreement.' And the full step four — 'You have all the information in the welcoming email. You can log in also to the Primal University community on school. Fill out the onboarding form before the call with Trevor.' Two things sit outside the checklist and are recorded as flags rather than scored here: the direct question about how the payment breaks down was answered without disclosing the instalment options that exist, and the rep gave the client his personal WhatsApp number to follow his progress.

objection_plays.detail: The documented script gap, in its most severe instance in this corpus. The prospect raised clinical fit three separate times and framed the last two as invitations to disqualify him: 'is this the right program for me?', 'is this potentially not a fit... you should go over here instead', and 'Do you know if Trevor's worked with anyone with a back injury?'. There is no scripted path, and the rep improvised three things, none of which addresses fit: an assertion of confidence ('I'm very confident that Trevor can help you'), a prevalence claim ('back injury, back pain, or something around back and hips is the most common thing that people are coming in with'), and a deferral to the post-payment onboarding call. This is not primarily a rep failure — the playbook has no clinical branch, no screening question, no escalation path and no disqualification criterion — but the outcome is that a man in a back brace with a ruptured disc bought a loaded ballistic training programme without a single clinical question being asked. The script needs a hard stop here, not a better word track.

The trigger fired — 'maybe I should wait two weeks so that my back can heal up from this recent flare-up' — and the rep ran a partial timing play, first conceding a week ('we can set the meeting, like, in a week or something like that. We'll get you, like, we secure the spot') and then reversing into an earlier start ('Or even you can meet with Trevor earlier, and he will give you something to work with before'). None of the scripted OD moves were used. Record this as a script safety gap rather than a coaching point: OD is written for a scheduling or busyness objection, and running any version of it against a medically motivated delay is the wrong response. The playbook gives the rep no way to tell those two triggers apart.

Second gap: the prospect asked to speak to the coach before committing money — 'is it okay for me to meet Trevor first before finalizing the payment? Or do I need to finalize the payment before?' There is no play for a buyer who wants to validate fit with the practitioner pre-purchase. The rep answered 'That's the process that we have' and the prospect accepted it. On a call where the open question was clinical safety, this is the moment the two gaps compound: the only person who could answer his question was behind the paywall.

No money objection arose. The prospect asked one logistics question about payment structure at minute forty and did not push back on the number at any point. Recorded as absent so it is not read as an unhandled trigger.

notes: Score the process honestly and separately from the money: P1, P4 and P11 are the best in the batch, P11 is textbook including the on-call signature that nobody else got, and the nutrition discovery was genuinely skilful. Then note what the process is not equipped to do. Every structural failure on this call sits on the same axis. P2c was never asked, so nothing forced the clinical conversation. P5 was skipped, so there was no phase to return to. P6c was missed, so three separate hesitations — all of them medical — were treated as buying signals to be moved past. And the only real objection on the call has no play at all. The coaching point for this rep is narrow and specific: hesitation about your body is not hesitation about your wallet, and the correct response to 'maybe I should wait two weeks so my back can heal' is never an earlier start date. The larger point is not a coaching point at all — it belongs to whoever owns the playbook. There is no clinical screen, no clearance question and no disqualification criterion anywhere in phases 1 through 11, and this call is what that costs.
